evidence.ACL: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Markedly edematous and enlarged with near complete/complete mid substance disruption.
evidence.MCL: minimal periligamentous edema could indicate a grade 1 sprain
evidence.Medial Meniscus: Small focus of surfacing signal abnormality (seen best on series 4, image 21 and series 6, image 19), which may represent a small undersurface tear at the junction of the body/posterior horn of the medial meniscus.
evidence.Medial OA: Slight cartilage heterogeneity and fraying along the central weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle
evidence.Lateral OA: Focal, mild cartilage fraying along the posterior/central lateral tibial plateau.
evidence.PF OA: Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.
evidence.Effusion: There is a small to moderate knee joint effusion.
evidence.Contusion: There are foci of bone marrow edema at the terminal sulcus of the lateral femoral condyle and posterior lateral tibial plateau consistent with a recent pivot shift type injury.
evidence.Fracture: No suspicious bone marrow signal abnormality is identified.
